title: The Rite of Spring Is One of My Favorite Scores of All Time
description: A look into Stravinsky's most famous (and infamous) work.
__content: # The Rite of Spring Is One of My Favorite Scores of All Time *The following post may contain copywrited material for the purpose of commentary, criticism, and education. No ownership is implied by that use.* *Cover Image: By Nicholas Roerich - from State Russian Museum, St. Petersburg at http://www.roerich.org/images/paintings/701809_043.jpg, Public Domain, Link* ## Background The Rite of Spring has been described as one of the most influential works of the modern era. Many have argued that it had completely transformed the trajectory of modern classical music into what we know it as today. # Further Exploration **Warning**: These first two videos are largely meant to be shorter introductions into The Rite of Spring with less overall depth. Some of the information in those videos comes from accounts that have been since **disputed or even debunked**. - [TED-ED](https://youtu.be/8FXA_8LR2IM?si=s-7BEtH3k5ZUFhGe) - [Classics Explained](https://youtu.be/6UKrmPoJv-k?si=ll77l7wlJUnGuN0a) This score analysis series by Thomas Goss also contains interviews and historical background, the latter of which has been **more thouroughly verified**. In particular, [one of the last videos](https://youtu.be/0x7znDvDLww?si=oydkaBKnfej6x5Cl) goes in-depth about the controversies and false accounts of The Rite of Spring. - [OrchestrationOnline: Analysis by Thomas Goss](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL7C2C0FC5318C4861)
